clinician.trajectory_summary: A 58-year-old African American male presented with abdominal distention, early satiety, and left flank pain. Initial CT imaging revealed a large (22 x 13 cm) left renal mixed echogenic lesion with diffuse fat and soft tissue elements suspicious for a giant renal angiomyolipoma. The patient underwent selective arterial embolization to reduce tumor size prior to surgical consultation. Subsequently, a radical left nephrectomy with 2 cm margins was performed. Histopathology from resection confirmed the tumor histologic type as well-differentiated liposarcoma (WDL) histologic grade 1. Microscopic examination showed the tumor abutting but not invading adjacent kidney tissue, composed of mature adipocytes with fibrotic stroma and spindle cells. The postoperative course was uncomplicated with discharge on day five and favorable recovery at one-week follow-up. No long-term follow-up data was available.
